items.definition:
to provide with a quality, ability, or asset
Nature endowed her with great musical talent.

sign or give formal consent to (a treaty, contract, or agreement), making it officially valid
The member states need to ratify the new treaty.

call people together for a meeting; assemble
The committee will convene next week to discuss the proposals.

to travel across or through
They had to traverse the entire mountain range.

to confer or present (an honor, right, or gift)
The queen will bestow a knighthood upon him for his service.

be mistaken or incorrect; make a mistake
To err is human, to forgive divine.

To create difficulties for someone or something, resulting in delay or obstruction.
Bad weather can hinder travel plans.

fill; pervade; soak
The tea leaves infuse the water with flavor.

contaminate; spoil
The scandal will taint his reputation.

decorate
She adorned her hair with flowers.

To harm the good reputation of.
The scandal served to discredit the politician.

To spread over or occupy (a place) in large numbers; to exceed (a limit or cost)
The weeds have overrun the garden.

to support (an organization or activity) financially
The government decided to subsidize public transport.

to refuse to give (something that is due to or is desired by another)
The company decided to withhold payment until the work was completed.

to surround (a place) with armed forces in order to capture it or force its surrender
The army decided to besiege the castle for several weeks.

to make something longer
The artist tried to elongate the figures in the painting.

to make poor
Years of war can impoverish a nation.

restore (someone or something) to their former position or state
The company decided to reinstate the old policy.

compete eagerly with someone in order to achieve something
The two teams will vie for the championship.

increase the volume of (sound), especially using an amplifier; enlarge upon or add details to (a story or statement)
The microphone will amplify your voice.

To yearn to possess or have (something).
She coveted her neighbor's beautiful garden.

represent; give tangible form to
The new building will embody the spirit of modern architecture.

hinder; restrain; prevent
Fear can inhibit people from expressing their true feelings.

to treat (a person, group, or concept) as insignificant or peripheral
Society tends to marginalize those who are different.

to feel deep respect or admiration for (something)
Many people revere him as a national hero.

call on (a deity or spirit) or cite (an authority) in support of an argument
He decided to invoke his right to remain silent.

to hinder or impede the movement or progress of
Heavy snow will hamper rescue efforts.

to hold and use (a weapon or tool); to exercise (power or influence)
He wielded the sword with great skill.

to arrest; to understand
The police were able to apprehend the suspect.

to make a loud, harsh cry (like a donkey)
We heard the donkey bray loudly from the field.

to establish (an attitude, habit, or belief) so firmly that change is very difficult or unlikely
The habit of daily exercise became deeply entrenched in his routine.

to cover thinly with gold; to give a specious or attractive appearance to
They decided to gild the frame of the old mirror.

To stimulate one's own genitals for sexual pleasure.
Some sex education classes explain why people masturbate.

To cause (people, opinions, etc.) to separate into opposing groups.
The issue has polarized public opinion.

To establish or decide in advance.
The outcome of the game was predetermined.

diminish or reduce in thickness toward one end
The road began to taper off into a narrow path.

find something out for certain; make sure of
We need to ascertain the facts before making a decision.

interpret (a word or action) in a particular way
His silence was construed as an admission of guilt.

to move power away from a central point
The company decided to decentralize its operations.

to destroy completely
The goal is to eradicate poverty.

imprison
The court decided to incarcerate the criminal for ten years.

to appear or claim to be or do something, especially falsely
The document purports to be a will.

to arrange into groups
The shopkeeper began to assort the different types of candies.

to reach a climax
The long negotiations culminated in a peace treaty.

to spread or cause to spread over a wide area or among a large number of people
The scent of flowers diffused through the room.

to make something seem important or impressive
He refused to dignify the accusations with a response.

to arrange or control the elements of a complex situation to produce a desired effect
The director managed to orchestrate a flawless performance.

to say something again or a number of times, typically for emphasis or clarity
Let me reiterate my main point: safety is our top priority.

to exist in large numbers or amounts
The rivers here abound with fish and other wildlife.

to put (someone) to death by nailing or binding them to a cross
Historically, some criminals were crucified as a form of execution.

to remove from office suddenly and forcefully
The king was deposed by a military coup last year.

remove by cutting out
The editor decided to excise the irrelevant paragraph from the article.

develop feathers for flight
The young birds will fledge and leave the nest soon.

to give nuances to; to make subtle distinctions
The artist carefully nuanced the colors in the painting.

provide or serve as clear evidence of
The ancient ruins attest to the city's former glory.

understand deeply
I can't fathom why he would do such a thing.

to secretly enter and become part of
The spy managed to infiltrate the enemy organization.

to express sorrow or regret
She lamented the loss of her youth.

to drain away from a solid by percolation
Rain can leach nutrients from the soil.

To carry out or commit (a harmful, illegal, or immoral action).
The criminals managed to perpetrate the robbery without being caught.

to greatly dismay or horrify
The news of the disaster appalled everyone.

to alienate, to separate
The argument caused him to estrange himself from his family.

Bring back to life
They hope to resurrect the ancient language.

to isolate
He decided to seclude himself from society.
